turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having pain (about 7/10), mainly in my right and left ankle and also my right and left thighs, and it feels tedious, sensitive, tugging, heavy, and sharp. I also have swelling around my right ankle, left thigh, and on the dorsal aspect of both feet, plus the sole of my left foot.

Do you have a history of heart failure, kidney disease, liver disease, blood clots, cancer, or are you pregnant/postpartum?
Yes—I have had deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and I have liver cirrhosis. I also have a known issue with one of my heart valves.

I don’t know.

[DDX] Volume overload/edema from cirrhosis or cardiac valvular disease, recurrent or bilateral deep vein thrombosis, lymphedema, cellulitis/soft-tissue infection, inflammatory arthritis

The bilateral foot/ankle swelling plus swelling in other body areas makes a systemic fluid-retention cause most likely, especially with known cirrhosis and heart valve disease. A recurrent DVT still needs consideration because of your history and thigh involvement, though symmetric swelling is a bit less typical. Infection and inflammatory causes are less supported but still possible.

Because DVT and heart-related fluid overload can be serious, you should get urgent in-person evaluation today, especially if you have any chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, or rapidly worsening swelling/pain. Likely tests would include leg venous ultrasound, CBC/CMP, liver/kidney tests, coagulation studies, and assessment for heart failure/volume overload.
